module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 862

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/862](https://www.erdosproblems.com/862)
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [SaTh15] Saxton, David and Thomason, Andrew, *Hypergraph containers*. Invent. Math. (2015),
  925-992.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos862

/--
$A_1(N)$, the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
-/
noncomputable def numMaximalSidonSets (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {A : Finset ℕ | A ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ Set.IsMaximalSidonSetIn (A : Set ℕ) N}.ncard

/--
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) < 2^{o(N^{1/2})}?$$

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean"]
theorem erdos_862.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    (fun N : ℕ => Real.logb 2 (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) > 2^{N^c}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean"]
theorem erdos_862.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((N : ℝ) ^ c) < (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that
the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least $2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each
Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each maximal Sidon set contains at most
$2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_862.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (((0.16 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≤ (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos862

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether A_1(N) < 2^{o(N^{1/2})}. Erdős's original (15) in [Er92c, p.39] is phrased 'for every ε > 0', i.e. A_1(n) < 2^{ε n^{1/2}} for large n. The Lean instead states `(fun N => Real.logb 2 (numMaximalSidonSets N)) =o[atTop] (fun N => N^(1/2))`, a little-o statement about log₂ A_1(N) with a non-strict bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A_1(N) ≥ 1 for every N, since a Sidon subset of maximum cardinality is maximal; I proved this as `one_le_numMaximalSidonSets`. Hence log₂ A_1(N) ≥ 0. (⇒) If A_1(N) < 2^{f(N)} eventually with f = o(√N), then 0 ≤ log₂ A_1(N) < f(N), so log₂ A_1 = O(f) = o(√N). (⇐) Take f(N) = log₂ A_1(N) + 1: this is still o(√N) because constants are o(√N), and A_1(N) < 2A_1(N) = 2^{f(N)}. The ε-form is the definition of little-o after taking logarithms; strict versus non-strict does not matter because ε is arbitrary and √N > 0. Both directions are proved in Lean for any a : ℕ → ℕ with a ≥ 1 (`lt_two_pow_littleO_iff`, `eps_form_iff`).

reformulations.difference: The source states A_1(N) ≥ 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}. The Lean states: for every ε > 0, eventually 2^{(0.16 − ε)·N^{1/2}} ≤ A_1(N).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (⇐) Given g → 0 with A_1(N) ≥ 2^{(0.16+g(N))√N} eventually: g(N) > −ε eventually, and 2^x is monotone. (⇒) Take g(N) = min(0, log₂A_1(N)/√N − 0.16). Then g ≤ 0, the ε-bounds give g ≥ −ε eventually, so g → 0, and 2^{(0.16+g(N))√N} ≤ 2^{log₂ A_1(N)} = A_1(N). Proved in Lean as `lower_form_iff` for any a : ℕ → ℕ with a ≥ 1.

review.notes:
I found no defects. All three theorems and the definition state the source's claims.

Checks I ran (all Lean proofs compile without `sorry`):
1. `numMaximalSidonSets N` equals a decidable `Finset.filter` count (lemma `key`). By `decide`/`native_decide`, N = 0, 3, 7, 12, 14 give 1, 3, 20, 176, 294. These match OEIS A325879 (maximal Sidon subsets of {1..n}). A list-based count matches A325879 for every n from 0 to 18.
2. A_1(N) ≥ 1 for all N (a maximum-cardinality Sidon subset is maximal).
3. The `lower_bound` variant implies ¬(log₂ A_1 = o(√N)), which is what `answer(False)` in part (i) asserts. It also implies ∃ c > 0 with 2^{N^c} < A_1(N) eventually (c = 1/4), which is what `answer(True)` in part (ii) asserts. The erdosproblems forum records the same answers: first question negative, second positive.

Source check: [Er92c, p.39] defines a Sidon sequence a_1 < … < a_k ≤ n as maximal if no t with 0 < t ≤ n can be added keeping it Sidon. That is inclusion-maximality in [1, n], exactly `Set.IsMaximalSidonSetIn`. Erdős's gloss 'i.e. every 1 ≤ t ≤ n can be written as a_i + a_j − a_r' leaves out the midpoint case 2t = a_i + a_j. The primary definition, erdosproblems.com, and the Saxton–Thomason resolution all use ordinary inclusion-maximality, as the file does.

The OCR layer did not capture the display formula of (15), only its label. The surrounding text is 'I would expect that (15) for every ε > 0, but (16) A_1(n) > 2^{n^c} for some c > 0'. That fits the site's rendering A_1(N) < 2^{o(N^{1/2})}, and a bound of the form 2^{n^ε} would contradict (16). The file follows the site's statement.

Part (ii) reads 'for some c > 0' as 'for all sufficiently large N'. Requiring it for all N would fail for every c, since A_1(1) = 1 < 2 = 2^{1^c}. A weaker 'infinitely many N' reading would also get the answer yes, so the reading does not change the answer.

Status: the file says `research solved` with a formal_proof for parts i and ii, and erdosproblems.com says 'SOLVED (LEAN)'; these agree. The linked plby proof uses {0,…,N−1} instead of {1,…,N} (a translate with the same count) and the natural log. It proves unconditional versions of both parts. Its main theorem gives ln A_1(N)/√N ≥ c for every c < ½·ln(5/4), which is log₂ A_1(N) ≥ (0.16096 − o(1))√N. So it also implies the `lower_bound` variant; that variant could optionally carry the same formal_proof attribute. It is already tagged solved, so this is not a status issue.

Side remark, outside this file: erdosproblems.com's metadata links problem 862 to OEIS A382395. That sequence counts maximum-size Sidon sets, not maximal ones (e.g. a(4) = 2, while A_1(4) = 3). A325879 is the matching sequence. The Lean file does not cite OEIS, so this does not affect it.
